findings.statement: The predeclared exact-rank degree-2 GF(2)^2 decoder is consistent on complete fresh 6x3-k3: 36,569 T2-O equations and zero contradictions.

The same fresh carrier strongly falsifies degree one with 520 contradictions, so the degree-2 pass is not vacuous and is not inherited from a geometry where affine composition already happened to work.
Degree two now removes every exact-rank affine contradiction in all three demanding carriers tested under the frozen model class: derivation carriers 5x3-k3 and 4x4-k4 plus fresh wider 6x3-k3.

The bounded evidence now supports a serious rank-graded quadratic GF(2)^2 evaluator hypothesis for T2-O component parity. This is stronger than the earlier late-XOR hypothesis because it identifies the first interaction order required by explicit falsifiers.

Full quadratic expansion is far from minimal: on fresh 6x3 it introduces 11,286 pair variables, yet the matrix rank rises only 472 above the degree-1 model. The next discovery target is the low-dimensional interaction subspace, not more polynomial degree.

Decompose the quadratic rank gain by exact rank and identify the smallest structurally generated interaction coordinates spanning the value-relevant second-order subspace before fitting sparse coefficients.

nonclaims: This is not a standard-7x6 theorem.
This does not establish that all geometries have polynomial degree at most two.
This does not make the full pair-feature expansion a satisfactory final D_G.
This does not identify canonical pair coefficients.
next_question: What low-dimensional exact-rank interaction subspace carries the second-order information that the full pair expansion redundantly represents?
